headline: SpaceX reached a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in GPU financing
body: SpaceX has reached a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data center equipment, according to a regulatory filing. Under the agreement, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management will buy the chips and server hardware and lease the equipment to SpaceX, and SpaceX expects the deal to close by year-end, subject to closing conditions.
note: TechCrunch says the lease gives SpaceX another way to fund AI spending without relying solely on traditional debt markets.

evidence.text: SpaceX has reached a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data center equipment, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing Monday .
Under the agreement, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, the New York-based private equity giant, will buy the chips and related server hardware, then lease the equipment to SpaceX.
SpaceX expects the deal to close by year-end, subject to closing conditions, with leases starting in the first half of 2027 as the GPUs and related equipment arrive.
The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.
